item.title: About
item.description:
I’m a systems and infrastructure engineer with interests spanning data centre networking and machine learning infrastructure. I graduated with a BSc in Computer Science from Trinity College Dublin.

I enjoy going deep on problems at the intersection of these — how networks behave under distributed AI workloads, why systems fail in ways that are hard to see, and how to build tooling that makes the invisible visible.

Most of my work lives at the systems layer. I built KubeScope, a kernel-level network observability platform using eBPF and Cilium that captures East-West traffic flows in containerised distributed systems without sidecar proxies. I’ve also been researching congestion control failure modes in AI training fabrics — studying how ECN behaves under GPU collective incast patterns, where the failure modes are and why they’re hard to detect in production.

item.title: Congestion Control Breakdown in AI Training Networks
item.description: ECN incast collapse at 4:1 sender ratio — reproducing the instability Meta observed abandoning DCQCN at 400G scale.
